Henderson Landscaping Services
Using winter to plan next year’s garden

Winter is an ideal time to step back and decide where your time and budget will make the biggest difference.

1. Review the year just gone
- Look through any photos you took in spring and summer.
- Make a quick list: what worked well, what was disappointing, what felt like hard work.
- Note any recurring problems: shade, waterlogging, privacy, clutter, lack of seating.

2. Prioritise by impact, not just cost
- Tidy, healthy lawns and hedges often transform how a garden feels day to day.
- Improving one key area (for example, a seating terrace) can be better than doing lots of small bits everywhere.
- Consider ongoing maintenance when choosing projects.

3. Decide what you can do yourself
- Simple tasks: basic weeding, mulching, light pruning, painting small timberwork.
- Jobs to consider delegating: major pruning, drainage, full lawn renovation, large hedge reductions.

4. When a design or planning consultation helps
- If you feel stuck or keep changing your mind.
- If the garden has several issues at once (levels, drainage, planting, access).
- If you’re budgeting for a bigger project and want a phased, realistic roadmap.

We offer both online and on-site consultations and can help you prioritise a sensible sequence of improvements for the year ahead.
